messages.content: "Can you tell me the net worth of the famous footballer Lionel Messi in Euros? After that, I would like to know the net worth of the basketball player LeBron James in British Pounds. Also, I'm curious about the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person who weighs 85 kilograms and is 180 centimeters tall using the metric system. Lastly, could you calculate the BMI of another person who weighs 200 pounds and is 6 feet 2 inches tall using the imperial system?"

function.name: calculate_bmi
function.description: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

weight.description: Weight of the person in kilograms.

height.description: Height of the person in centimeters.

unit.description: Optional parameter to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric' systems. Default is 'metric'.

function.name: celebrity_net_worth_get
function.description: Get the total net worth of a sports celebrity based on most recent data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the sports celebrity.

currency.description: The currency in which the net worth will be returned. Default is 'USD'.

For BMI metric: weight 85 kg, height 180 cm, unit default metric. For BMI imperial: weight 200 lbs, height 6 ft 2 in. But the calculate_bmi function expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters. It also has optional unit param. But it doesn't accept pounds or feet. So we need to convert manually? The function only accepts weight in kilograms and height in centimeters. But we can pass weight in kilograms and height in centimeters. For imperial, we need to convert 200 pounds to kilograms: 200 lb * 0.45359237 = 90.7185 kg approx. Height 6 ft 2 in: 6 ft = 72 inches + 2 = 74 inches. 1 inch = 2.54 cm, so 74*2.54=187.96 cm. So weight 90.7185 kg, height 187.96 cm. Then we can call calculate_bmi with those values. Or we can use unit param? The function signature says optional unit param to choose between 'imperial' and 'metric', default metric. But the function expects weight in kilograms and height in centimeters regardless. So maybe the unit param is irrelevant. We'll just call with weight and height in metric units. So we need to call calculate_bmi twice: first with weight 85, height 180. Second with weight 90.7185, height 187.96.

We need to output the results. We should call the functions sequentially. Let's do that.
